user_rationale: Brief explanation of why user chose this strategy (2-3 sentences)

plugin_based.description: Modular components with Protocol-based interfaces and dependency injection
plugin_based.when_to_use: High extensibility requirements, runtime plugin loading, multi-environment deployment, need for loose coupling
pros: Maximum flexibility - swap implementations at runtime
Multi-environment deployment (prod, test, dev use different plugins)
cons: Requires Protocol + DI patterns (more upfront design)
Team needs to understand modern patterns

domain_based.when_to_use: Clear domain boundaries, low coordination requirements, CRUD-heavy operations
pros: Easy to understand for domain experts
cons: Coordination logic becomes distributed state management

workflow_based.when_to_use: High coordination requirements, cross-domain workflows, workflow-heavy operations
pros: Common workflows self-contained in one service
Fewer service-to-service calls for common operations
Easier to reason about workflow state
cons: May duplicate some domain logic across services

hybrid.description: Mix of plugin, workflow, and domain services based on specific needs
hybrid.when_to_use: Large, complex systems with varied requirements - some need extensibility, some need coordination, some are simple domains
pros: Best of all strategies - tailored per service
cons: Need clear architectural guidelines per service type
Requires strong architectural discipline and documentation

plugin_based.service_decomposition: Identify swappable components, define Protocol interfaces, create plugin registries
plugin_based.coordination_pattern: Injected orchestrators - coordination logic provided via DI, swappable per environment
plugin_based.state_management: State managed via injected providers, multiple implementations per environment
plugin_based.integration_pattern: Protocol interfaces + Dependency Injection, plugin discovery at startup

domain_based.service_decomposition: Group functions by business domain (User, Product, Order, Payment)
domain_based.coordination_pattern: Distributed - services coordinate via events, sagas, or orchestration
domain_based.state_management: Each service owns its domain state

workflow_based.service_decomposition: Group functions by user workflow (Checkout, Inventory, Fulfillment)
workflow_based.coordination_pattern: Local - coordination state managed within workflow service
workflow_based.state_management: Workflow services own workflow state, may access shared domain state

hybrid.service_decomposition: Classify each service: plugin (extensible), workflow (coordination), or domain (shared capabilities)
hybrid.coordination_pattern: Mixed - injected for plugins, local for workflows, distributed for domains
hybrid.state_management: Per service type: injected providers (plugin), workflow state (workflow), domain state (domain)
hybrid.integration_pattern: Mixed - DI for plugins, orchestration for workflows, events for domains
hybrid.classification_guidance: Document why each service uses its pattern in service_architecture.json
